comments.content: When originalOrders is non-empty we reorder to originalOrders[0] and never re-add $qualifiedKeyName. If the first original order is not the key column, the query loses the key ordering required for chunked cursor pagination on PostgreSQL. The original implementation always forced $qualifiedKeyName first; now it is only used when originalOrders is empty.

Accessing $query->getQuery()->orders[0]['column'] without first ensuring orders exists will raise an undefined offset warning when the query has no orders. Use data_get / count check before indexing, e.g. data_get($query->getQuery()->orders, '0.column').
